description: Describe a space and receive the works that fit it, each with the measurement behind the suggestion and its curatorial capsule. Room light, viewing distance, screen size, attention and movement are measured; collection, resolution, orientation, colour and budget are hard limits, and a work that may be rotated counts for the other orientation. If nothing fits, it says which requirement leaves nothing instead of offering the nearest thing. For catalogue requests that do not concern a physical space — including requests for calm, slow, dark, bright or otherwise measured works — use the relevant catalogue tool directly. Do not ask for screen or room details. Do not promise to search: search first, then answer with the returned works, identifiers, availability and other requested details. If the request is clear enough to search, do not ask a clarifying question before searching; make a reasonable catalogue query and state any meaningful limitation afterwards. This catalogue rule does not apply to space recommendations. For any request about what work would suit a physical space, this space rule overrides the catalogue rule above. Before naming a work or presenting any recommendation, establish the native screen resolution, orientation, screen size, viewing distance, whether the work should accompany or hold attention, and the effective light at the screen. Do not map “soft daylight”, “soft natural light”, “soft and diffused daylight” or similar wording to `dim` or `bright` automatically. Even when the room description mentions curtains, indirect light or no direct sun, ask whether the image area on the screen is effectively dim or bright and whether the light can be controlled. If any required space datum is missing, do not call `recommend_for_space`, do not use another catalogue tool to name a provisional work, and do not present a work as a calculated recommendation. You may ask one concise clarifying question or offer a clearly conditional orientation without naming a work. Only after all six data points are established may you map the light to `dim` or `bright`, call `recommend_for_space`, name a returned work, and describe the match as measured. Never say that a work was measured for “soft daylight” when the tool calculated it for `dim` or `bright`.
